blocks.title: Session 1 · Foundations and Angles
content: Build a precise vocabulary, then use relationships to solve unknown angles.

blocks.title: Predict: use geometric notation and distinguish congruence from similarity
content: What information is lost if a ray’s endpoint is written second?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: use geometric notation and distinguish congruence from similarity
content: Point, line, and plane are accepted undefined terms.
Order matters in ray and angle notation.
Congruent figures have equal size and shape; similar figures have proportional corresponding sides.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: use geometric notation and distinguish congruence from similarity
content: Interpret $\overleftrightarrow{AB}$, $\overrightarrow{AB}$, $\overline{AB}$, and $\angle ABC$.
steps: $\overleftrightarrow{AB}$ extends in both directions; $\overrightarrow{AB}$ starts at A.
In $\angle ABC$, B is the vertex.

blocks.title: You Try: use geometric notation and distinguish congruence from similarity
content: Identify $\overleftrightarrow{AB}$, $\overrightarrow{AB}$, $\overline{AB}$, and $\angle ABC$, including endpoints or vertex.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.
answer: $\overleftrightarrow{AB}$ is a line; $\overrightarrow{AB}$ is a ray with endpoint A.
$\overline{AB}$ is a segment with endpoints A and B; $\angle ABC$ has vertex B.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: use geometric notation and distinguish congruence from similarity
content: Do not reverse ray endpoints.
Similarity does not imply equal side lengths.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: use geometric notation and distinguish congruence from similarity
content: Explain the difference between congruence and similarity in one sentence.
instructor_notes: If more than 3 minutes behind, shorten discussion but preserve the next practice and feedback slides.

blocks.title: Predict: measure, classify, and relate angles
content: Can two obtuse angles be complementary? Explain.
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: measure, classify, and relate angles
content: Acute angles are below 90°, right angles equal 90°, obtuse angles lie between 90° and 180°, and straight angles equal 180°.
Vertical angles are congruent; a linear pair is supplementary.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: measure, classify, and relate angles
content: Two lines intersect and one angle is $47^\circ$. Find and classify the other three.
verification: Verify angle classifications and supplementary calculations.
steps: The pair is two acute vertical angles and two obtuse vertical angles.

blocks.title: You Try: measure, classify, and relate angles
content: Two intersecting lines create an angle of 68°. Find the other three angles.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.
answer: The vertical angle is 68°; each adjacent angle is 112°.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: measure, classify, and relate angles
content: Adjacent does not automatically mean supplementary.
Complementary means a sum of 90°, not equal measures.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Verify angle classifications and supplementary calculations.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: measure, classify, and relate angles
content: Given one angle at an intersection, describe how to find the other three.
instructor_notes: If more than 3 minutes behind, shorten discussion but preserve the next practice and feedback slides.

blocks.title: Predict: use parallel-line relationships to solve angle equations
content: When a transversal crosses parallel lines, which angle pairs must be equal?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: use parallel-line relationships to solve angle equations
content: Corresponding, alternate interior, and alternate exterior angles are congruent.
Same-side interior angles are supplementary.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: use parallel-line relationships to solve angle equations
content: Corresponding angles measure $(3x+10)^\circ$ and $(5x-20)^\circ$. Solve.

blocks.title: You Try: use parallel-line relationships to solve angle equations
content: Write and solve an equation for a same-side interior pair $(4x+8)^\circ$ and $(6x+12)^\circ$.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: use parallel-line relationships to solve angle equations
content: Name the relationship before writing the equation.
After solving x, substitute back to find the requested angle.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: use parallel-line relationships to solve angle equations
content: State the relationship-to-equation rule for equal and supplementary pairs.
instructor_notes: If more than 3 minutes behind, shorten discussion but preserve the next practice and feedback slides.

blocks.title: Session 2 · Polygons, Triangles, and Applications
content: Choose formulas strategically and justify every geometric relationship.

blocks.title: Predict: compute polygon angle sums and areas
content: Why is the exterior-angle sum always 360° for a convex polygon?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: compute polygon angle sums and areas
content: Interior-angle sum: $(n-2)180^\circ$.
Exterior-angle sum: $360^\circ$.
Compound-shape area comes from decomposing into familiar pieces.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: compute polygon angle sums and areas
content: Find an octagon’s interior-angle sum and the area of a trapezoid with bases 12 and 20 and height 7.
verification: Verify polygon angle formulas and all area computations.
steps: Angle measure uses degrees; area uses square units.

blocks.title: You Try: compute polygon angle sums and areas
content: A regular polygon has exterior angle 24°. Find the number of sides and each interior angle.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: compute polygon angle sums and areas
content: Use n for the number of sides, not the number of triangles drawn.
Subtract holes only after computing the outer area.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Verify polygon angle formulas and all area computations.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: compute polygon angle sums and areas
content: Describe a decision process for selecting a polygon-area formula.

blocks.title: Predict: select and apply triangle area and Pythagorean formulas
content: What information determines whether to use $A=bh/2$, Heron’s formula, or the equilateral formula?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: select and apply triangle area and Pythagorean formulas
content: Use $A=bh/2$ when a base and perpendicular height are known.
Use Heron’s formula with three sides.
For an equilateral triangle, $A=s^2\sqrt3/4$.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: select and apply triangle area and Pythagorean formulas
content: Find the area of an equilateral triangle with side 1600 km.
verification: Verify Heron, equilateral, and Pythagorean calculations.
steps: The exact radical form is preferred unless an approximation is requested.

blocks.title: You Try: select and apply triangle area and Pythagorean formulas
content: Find the area of a triangle with sides 7, 8, and 9 using Heron’s formula.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: select and apply triangle area and Pythagorean formulas
content: Height must be perpendicular to the chosen base.
The Pythagorean theorem applies only to right triangles.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Verify Heron, equilateral, and Pythagorean calculations.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: select and apply triangle area and Pythagorean formulas
content: Name the given information that triggers each triangle-area method.

blocks.title: Predict: solve similarity proportions and convert navigation angles
content: How does vertex order prevent a similarity proportion from using mismatched sides?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: solve similarity proportions and convert navigation angles
content: Corresponding vertices must remain in the same order.
DMS conversion uses 60 minutes per degree and 60 seconds per minute.
One nautical mile corresponds to one minute of latitude.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: solve similarity proportions and convert navigation angles
content: Solve $6/9=10/x$, then convert $45^\circ22'18''$ to decimal degrees.
verification: Verify similarity proportions and all DMS conversions.
steps: Corresponding sides stay in the same order and DMS uses factors of 60.

blocks.title: You Try: solve similarity proportions and convert navigation angles
content: Convert $73.625^\circ$ to DMS. A larger similar triangle has scale factor $3/2$ from a smaller triangle whose corresponding side is 14; find the larger side.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: solve similarity proportions and convert navigation angles
content: Do not pair noncorresponding sides.
Carry minutes before seconds when converting DMS.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Verify similarity proportions and all DMS conversions.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: solve similarity proportions and convert navigation angles
content: Explain how proportional reasoning connects similar triangles and map/navigation scale.
